scope_update: Final user constraint permits physical placement using existing hardware operations only. New sparsity masks, precision methods, decoder/ABI changes and operators are excluded.

sources.title: SLIM: A Heterogeneous Accelerator for Edge Inference of Sparse Large Language Model via Adaptive Thresholding
sources.version: arXiv 2507.09201v1; TECS DOI independently identified, journal publication date not verified here
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
sources.github_status: No author artifact verified through manuscript links or exact-title GitHub searches.
sources.read_depth: Read methods 5.4, 6.1, 6.3, evaluation model table and discussion 7.6 in author preprint. ACM full text returned 403.
sources.evidence: Fused gate/up/down neuron vectors, page-aligned vector packing, even die distribution, MoE DeepSeek/Mixtral evaluation. Discussion explicitly proposes aligning consecutive physical pages on a common wordline for multi-plane reads.
sources.novelty_threat: Neuron-level MoE sparsity, fused-vector page packing, die balancing and generic multipane alignment are already described.
sources.constraint_status: Its existing architecture may be studied as a separate hardware case. Its fused FFN and column skipping cannot be added to AiF as a placement-only change.

sources.title: Neuralink: Fast on-Device LLM Inference with Neuron Co-Activation Linking
sources.alternate_arxiv_title: Neuralink: Fast LLM Inference on Smartphones with Neuron Co-Activation Linking
sources.version: 2410.19274v3, 2025-10-12; v1 independently verified as Ripple, not a separate work
sources.github_status: No author repository verified. Author publication page links the paper, not a code artifact.
sources.read_depth: Read sections 4 and 5 and primary metadata/version history.
sources.evidence: Coactivation graph, nearest-link merging toward a Hamiltonian ordering, contiguous access collapse and segment caching. Bundling accounts for gate/up/down correspondence.
sources.novelty_threat: Generic coactivation neuron ordering and larger contiguous logical reads are direct prior art; NAND die/page placement is not established by the inspected method.

sources.title: VLM in a flash: I/O-Efficient Sparsification of Vision-Language Model via Neuron Chunking
sources.venue: NeurIPS 2025, as stated by author repository
sources.read_depth: Read sections 3.1–3.3, evaluation setup and official repository README.
sources.evidence: Profiles chunk-size read cost, chooses chunks by importance per latency, and applies frequency sorting; authors report frequency ordering competitive with coactivation ordering.
sources.novelty_threat: Neuron grouping, hot/cold ordering and an I/O-aware latency objective are already present. Selection changes the mask, so a fixed-mask physical-layout comparison must separate that benefit.
sources.constraint_status: New sparsification is excluded by final user constraint.

sources.title: PowerInfer-2: Fast Large Language Model Inference on a Smartphone
sources.version: 2406.06282v1 methods read; latest primary abstract identifies v3 dated 2024-12-12
sources.github_status: Original SJTU-IPADS/PowerInfer redirects here. A complete PowerInfer-2-specific artifact was not verified.
sources.read_depth: Read neuron-aware execution, I/O bundling and cache discussion; repository inspected for project identity.
sources.evidence: Neuron clusters account for heterogeneous compute and I/O, corresponding gate/up/down weights are bundled, and cache misses trigger flash loads.
sources.novelty_threat: Neuron-level hybrid execution and I/O bundling cannot be treated as new; cold-neuron locality needs measurement after hot caching.

sources.title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory
sources.read_depth: Section 3, including closest-friend coactivation bundling, read in previous literature pass.
sources.evidence: Row/column bundling and windowing reduce flash I/O. Further coactivation bundling was evaluated with duplication and did not improve the tested setup.
sources.novelty_threat: A negative result already exists for naive coactivation bundling; repeat it as a baseline, not a new premise.

sources.title: Swarm: Co-Activation Aware KVCache Offloading Across Multiple SSDs
sources.venue: arXiv version verified; author homepage lists related Octopus/ATC 2026 but equivalence is not assumed
sources.evidence: Coactivation clusters with overlap/replication, round-robin entry striping across SSDs, and replica-aware bucket balancing for selected query sets.
sources.novelty_threat: Coactivation grouping followed by distributing selected work across parallel devices is direct prior, even though the data is KV rather than weights.

sources.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Sparse Attention with High-Bandwidth Flash for Efficient Long-Context Inference
sources.github_status: No author code verified; unrelated GitHub projects named Splash must not be matched.
sources.evidence: Groups co-selected tokens into pages, stripes consecutive pages across all planes, places paired key/value pages on different planes, and caps selection per plane to k rounds.
sources.novelty_threat: Page granularity plus parallel-plane placement is already an explicit co-design objective. Its plane-specific selection changes the chosen pages, so it is not a fixed-mask layout result.

sources.title: A Hypergraph Based Approach to Declustering Problems
sources.read_depth: Read definitions 1–6, generalized objective and greedy placement sections 2–3 in institutional full text, plus conclusion.
sources.evidence: Queries are hyperedges with frequencies, items have different sizes and retrieval times, capacity is constrained, and objective is expected maximum summed item time per device. Retrieval time is explicitly allowed to be a step function of item size.
sources.novelty_threat: Selected-set hypergraphs, min-max device work, capacity constraints and replacing bytes with a rounded service cost are old abstractions. New work must change/solve a real NAND-specific feasibility issue or matrix partitioning problem.

sources.title: Query-Log Aware Replicated Declustering
sources.read_depth: Institutional full text opened; abstract, problem description and method overview read. Not all experiments audited.
sources.evidence: Jointly chooses which items to copy and their disk assignment from query logs under capacity and limited replication; recursive partitioning and refinement.
sources.novelty_threat: Selective partial copies conditioned on co-request patterns are already explicit. Adding MoE terminology does not create a new mechanism.

sources.title: Generalized Optimal Response Time Retrieval of Replicated Data from Storage Arrays
sources.read_depth: Author full text opened; abstract and problem/method summary read. Proofs and all evaluations not independently checked.
sources.evidence: Optimal replica retrieval via LP and maximum flow with heterogeneous devices, initial loads and delays; also an online heuristic.
sources.novelty_threat: The replicated-flow resource comparator developed in the local experiment is a baseline instance of a known scheduling abstraction, not a novel algorithm.

sources.title: Physically Addressed Queueing (PAQ): Improving Parallelism in Solid State Disks
sources.read_depth: Author primary PDF abstract and university publication metadata read; not full method audit.
sources.evidence: Exposes physical request addresses, groups compatible operations, and packs inter-request NAND transactions to use multipane mode.
sources.novelty_threat: Recognizing legal physical parallelism and transaction packing is established SSD work; a static expert layout needs a distinct sustained benefit.

sources.title: Sprinkler: Maximizing Resource Utilization in Many-Chip Solid State Disks
sources.read_depth: Read primary PDF abstract and introduction; not full method audit.
sources.evidence: Schedules by physical resource layout, relaxes request-order dependencies, and combines flash work to improve transaction locality and resource use.
sources.novelty_threat: Physical-address-aware NAND scheduling and resource utilization are not new claims.

sources.title: GEMQ: Global Expert-Level Mixed-Precision Quantization for MoE LLMs
sources.read_depth: Read official PMLR metadata, preprint section 4.1 and author repository README/solver description.
sources.evidence: Global expert bit allocation under a bit budget, quantization error importance and router fine-tuning.
sources.constraint_status: Excluded by final placement-only user constraint; do not reopen as a proposed quantization contribution.

sources.title: Hardware-Aware Mixed-Precision Scheduling for Edge MoE Inference on GPU-NDP Systems
sources.read_depth: Official IEEE abstract obtained through indexed primary result. Direct full-text fetch failed; full paper not read.
sources.evidence: Gating-probability importance, bitwidth increments and hardware latency lookup-table mapping.
sources.name_correction: HAPS was a local shorthand, not a verified author acronym; do not use it as the formal method name.
sources.constraint_status: Excluded by final placement-only user constraint.

sources.title: NASiC: 3D NAND-based CAM-Selected Multibit CIM Architecture for Efficient On-Device Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference
sources.read_depth: Read primary abstract and architecture section outline; circuit proofs and simulation not audited.
sources.evidence: CAM-selected NAND CIM, dynamically selected experts and multibit cell/circuit changes.
sources.constraint_status: Analog/circuit mechanism differs from ordinary digital NAND reads; excluded as an existing-AiF placement-only candidate.
